identity.name: Patriarchate of Aquileia
alt_names: Temporal state of the Patriarchs of Aquileia

land.text: the Friulian lands, a Carolingian march from 828 reorganised into the March of Friuli, added to the March of Verona in 952, in which Henry IV vested Patriarch Sieghard with 'immediate comital rights' on 3 April 1077

predecessors.note: Cliopatria begins the Patriarchate only in 1260. The Friulian lands were carved out of the March of Verona in 1077 ('the remaining parts of the March of Verona' went to Liutold of Eppenstein, Patria del Friuli page); the march-of-verona dossier records the 1077 loss to this state. (Reviewer eu-13-i: slug changed from kingdom-of-italy, which is the 1861-1946 kingdom.)

land.text: Friuli, 'Venetians thus annexed the territory, depriving the Patriarch of Aquileia of his temporal powers'; Cliopatria's Venice shape of 1422 holds 26 of the 32 cells of the Patriarchate's 1407 shape

successors.note: Temporal authority ended on 7 July 1420; the Empire ceded the Domini di Terraferma to Venice as an Imperial fief in 1433 and Patriarch Ludovico Trevisan accepted the loss of his temporal estate in 1445.

capitals.name: Aquileia
capitals.note: Page silent on the earlier seat (the patriarchs also resided at Cividale); Aquileia is the see.

capitals.name: Udine
capitals.note: 'the state's capital moved to Udine from 1238'; another passage of the same page gives 1223.

correction.text: the Friulian lands of the patriarchal state

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1077-1208: Cliopatria begins the Patriarchate in 1260. On 3 April 1077 Henry IV vested the patriarch 'with immediate comital rights in the Friulian lands'; the page gives no extent beyond Friuli ('up to Cadore'), so the Friuli region stands in. No infobox area on the page.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1260 outline used for 1209-1259: Friuli with the Istrian march

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1209-1259: Friuli plus the Istrian march, which 'Aquileia regained in 1209' after the Andechs margraves were banned. Cliopatria's 1260 outline (Friuli, the Soča valley and a few interior Istrian cells) stands in for it.

8,915 km2: Friuli (Udine, Pordenone, Gorizia), the Goriska valley and three cells in interior Istria. The page names the same lands ('up to Cadore'; Istria regained in 1209) but draws no boundary, and gives no area.
9,006 km2: one more Istrian cell near 45.5 N 14.0 E than 1260 (91 km2). No page dates the change.

8,103 km2: all the Istrian cells and a Carnic cell are gone. The page has Venice occupy the western Istrian coast from Capodistria to Rovigno in the late 13th century and 'a peace concluded at Treviso' in 1291 leave Venice with it, so the loss fits 1291-1294; the page does not say that the Patriarch lost interior Istria then, and it lists Muggia, Labin and Plomin as Aquileian until 1420, which this outline omits.
8,335 km2: the same cells as 1294 with a re-drawn edge in the south (bbox to 45.17 N). Nothing on the pages explains it.

8,217 km2: the 1314 outline with the Carnic cell back and the two western cells on the Livenza near Oderzo (45.8 N 12.5-12.7 E) out. The page says only 'A recovery occurred during the rule of Bertrand (1334-1350)'; no territory is named.
8,125 km2: the Carnic cell out again. No page dates it; Patriarch Bertrand was killed in 1350.
8,171 km2: a re-drawn edge only (the same 30 cells as 1363).

union.text: Muggia, Labin and Plomin, the Aquileian possessions in Istria

correction.text: the 1407 shape plus Muggia, Labin and Plomin; years 1407-1418

keyframe_review.note: 8,333 km2: the two western Livenza cells return (32 cells, Friuli with the Goriska valley). It holds 1407-1418; Cividale falls on 23 July 1419 and Udine on 7 June 1420. The page lists Muggia, Labin and Plomin as Aquileian possessions surrendered in 1420, which Cliopatria's outline lacks.

union.text: Muggia, Labin and Plomin, the Aquileian possessions in Istria

minus.text: the 1407 shape plus Muggia, Labin and Plomin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1419: 'On 23 July 1419 the Venetians conquered Cividale, and then continued to advance further.'

union.text: Muggia, Labin and Plomin, the Aquileian possessions in Istria

minus.text: the 1407 shape plus Muggia, Labin and Plomin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1420 (to July): 'Udine fell to Venetians on 7 June 1420 after a long siege'; Gemona, San Daniele, Venzone and Tolmezzo fell after it, and on 7 July 1420 'Venice secularised the territory, ending the patriarch's temporal authority'. The shape holds until that date.

correction.text: the former patriarchal land of Friuli, which is Venice's from 1420; no temporal patriarchal state remains

keyframe_review.note: 1,681 km2 (six cells in the Soca valley around Tolmin, Bovec and Gradisca) in 1422-1439: the page says 'the secular territory of the patriarchs of Aquileia had been completely conquered by Venice in 1420' and that the patriarch's temporal authority ended on 7 July 1420, naming no land kept; 'minor possessions throughout Carniola and Carinthia' are undated. The Friulian land is Venetian from 1420 (Cliopatria's Venice shape has it from 1422). The six cells are unexplained and may be Gorizian or Venetian land.

correction.text: Friuli as Venetian land; the patriarch held no temporal state, the 1445 treaty only ratified the loss

keyframe_review.note: The same six cells, 1440-1449. Louis of Teck failed to invade Friuli in April and September 1422 and again in 1431 ('repelled by Venice'); in 1445 Patriarch Ludovico Trevisan, at the Council of Florence, 'accepted the loss of his temporal estate' for 5,000 ducats a year. The state had no land to draw after July 1420.

ledger.note: 1077: Henry IV makes the Patriarch of Aquileia count of Friuli. 'On 3 April 1077, Henry IV, at Pavia, vested Aquileian Patriarch Sieghard of Beilstein with immediate comital rights in the Friulian lands.' The page gives the Friulian lands, not a boundary; the Friuli region stands in.

1209: the patriarchs regain the Istrian march. 'Aquileia regained Istria in 1209', after the Andechs margraves (Dukes of Merania) were banned over the murder of Philip of Swabia; the Patria page: 'In 1209 the patriarchs regained the Istrian march from the Dukes of Merania'.
1238: the capital moves to Udine. 'the state's capital moved to Udine from 1238'; another passage of the same page gives 1223, so the year is the page's but disputed within it.

region.text: the western Istrian coast from Capodistria (Koper) to Rovigno (Rovinj)

ledger.note: 1291: Venice keeps the western Istrian coast. 'In the late 13th century Venice occupied the western Istrian coast from Capodistria (Koper) to Rovigno (Rovinj)' and 'a peace concluded at Treviso in 1291 left Venice' with it; the page does not name the parties. The March of Istria page: 'By mid-century most of the Istrian coast had been conquered by Venice'. Cliopatria's Istrian cells disappear in 1272-1294.

1411: war breaks out in Friuli. 'In 1411, those conflicts turned into a war which was to mark the end of the Patriarchal State': Cividale, backed by the Friulian communes, the Carraresi of Padua and Sigismund, against Udine, backed by Venice; an Imperial army captured Udine in December 1411 and Louis of Teck was enthroned in January 1412. The first Venetian conquest of ground is 1419.
1419: Venice takes Cividale. 'On 23 July 1419 the Venetians conquered Cividale, and then continued to advance further.'

region.text: Muggia, Labin and Plomin, the Aquileian possessions in Istria

ledger.note: 1420: Muggia, Labin and Plomin surrender to Venice. 'Muggia, Labin and Plomin, Aquileian possessions in Istria, surrendered to Venice' in 1420; the March of Istria page: after 1420 'most of Istria belonged to La Serenissima'.
1420: Udine falls to Venice. 'Udine fell to Venetians on 7 June 1420 after a long siege.'

region.text: Gemona, San Daniele, Venzone and Tolmezzo and the rest of the Patria del Friuli

ledger.note: 1420: Gemona, San Daniele, Venzone and Tolmezzo fall. 'After June 1420' per the page, which gives no dates; the whole of the Patria del Friuli outside Cividale and Udine goes to Venice.

1420: the Venetian war ends with the end of the patriarchs' temporal power. The page: on 7 July 1420 Venice 'secularised the territory, ending the patriarch's temporal authority'. Louis of Teck's attempts to return (April and September 1422, 1431) were repelled by Venice and are outside the state's life.

1420: the Patriarchal State of Friuli is annexed by Venice. 'Venetians thus annexed the territory, depriving the Patriarch of Aquileia of his temporal powers' (7 July 1420); in 1433 the Empire ceded the Domini di Terraferma to Venice as an Imperial fief, and in 1445 Patriarch Ludovico Trevisan accepted the loss of his temporal estate for 5,000 ducats a year ('The former state became part of the Republic of Venice as Patria del Friuli').

wars.name: War of the Patriarchal State of Friuli, 1411-1420
wars.outcome: A civil war between Cividale and Udine in 1411 (Udine captured by an Imperial army in December 1411) became a Venetian conquest: Cividale fell on 23 July 1419, Udine on 7 June 1420 and the patriarch's temporal power ended on 7 July 1420.
wars.note: The page gives no start year earlier than 1411 for the war; the 14th-century wars with Gorizia, Treviso and Padua are not on any page opened.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary of the Patria del Friuli; the outlines are Cliopatria's approximations and the Istrian edge is the softest.

sources.title: Patriarchate of Aquileia
sources.note: No infobox; Udine as capital from 1238, Bertrand 1334-1350, Udine 7 June 1420, 1445.

sources.title: Patria del Friuli

notes: Pages opened: 3 of the up to 5 budgeted. Cliopatria rows to correct: the Patriarchate begins in 1260 but the page dates its temporal state to 1077 (new keyframes 1077 and 1209); its end is 1449 in Cliopatria but 7 July 1420 on the page (the 1422-1449 residue of six Soca-valley cells is judged wrong: the page says the territory was 'completely conquered by Venice in 1420'); the Venetian Friuli begins 1420, not 1422; Muggia, Labin and Plomin are Aquileian until 1420 but Cliopatria draws no Istria after 1294 except in 1314-1343. Page silent: the boundary of the state; the 1260s-1390s wars with Gorizia, Treviso and Padua; the Torriani patriarchs; why Cliopatria's edges change in 1272, 1294, 1314, 1344, 1363, 1407 (Istrian, Carnic and Livenza cells, all under 250 km2 each); the six-cell remnant; the earlier seat before Udine (Aquileia assumed; Cividale was a residence); 1223 against 1238 for Udine; 1411 civil war counterparts (Cividale against Udine). The Patria page gives 7 July 1420, the Patriarchate page only 7 June (Udine). Needs dossiers: the March of Verona or Kingdom of Italy (predecessor), Dukes of Merania (Andechs), the Counts of Gorizia (not touched on the pages), and Muggia/Labin/Plomin. No ruler strip: the pages give only Sieghard (1068-1077), Bertrand (1334-1350), Louis of Teck (1412-1420) and Ludovico Trevisan (1445).
